strengths: The paper presents a simple, interpretable defense that suppresses selected attention-head contributions to the CLS token without fine-tuning model weights.

Results cover five model sizes and four typographic benchmarks. Reported ImageNet-100-Typo gains reach 19.60 percentage points, while accuracy changes on three clean classification benchmarks are generally small.

Layerwise probes and attention interventions provide complementary evidence that selected later-layer heads contribute to typographic sensitivity. The discussion acknowledges limitations for downstream systems using spatial tokens.
weaknesses: The central Typographic Attention Score is incorrectly defined in Equation 6: each attention weight cancels between numerator and denominator, making the score independent of the head. The dataset sum also lacks normalization despite the claimed [0,1] range. This may be a transcription error, but the published definition cannot produce the reported rankings. Figure 5's caption additionally reverses the meaning of alpha relative to Equation 8 and the plotted results.

Essential controls for the mechanistic contribution are missing. There are no matched random-head or layer-matched ablations, alternative ranking baselines, or controlled comparisons separating bottom-position preference from typography selectivity. Interventions demonstrate that the selected heads affect predictions, but do not establish a uniquely typography-specific circuit or the necessity of the proposed selection method.

Defense comparisons are insufficient: only Defense-Prefix is evaluated, on one model size, despite several relevant defenses being discussed. Defense-Prefix achieves 82.78% on Disentangling versus 65.00% for the proposed method and performs better on every attacked benchmark in Table 4. ImageNet-100-Typo is omitted from that comparison, and no measured runtime or memory comparison substantiates the efficiency advantage.

The security and deployment claims exceed the evaluation. Experiments use fixed classification benchmarks without adaptive attacks or systematic variation of text placement, appearance, and content. No VLM, retrieval, generation, or safety-critical application is evaluated; the acknowledged persistence of typography in spatial tokens particularly weakens the broad drop-in replacement claims.

Reproducibility is incomplete. Exact pretrained checkpoints, probe training and evaluation protocols, detailed synthetic-text generation settings, selected head identities, and an accessible release location are not provided. There are no repeated-run uncertainty estimates for the main accuracy results, which matters especially for the 180- and 110-image benchmarks.

Several interpretations are stronger than the evidence supports. Reduced linear-probe accuracy and PCA effective dimension do not establish that MLPs discard information, and improved clean-dataset transfer does not establish that causal targeting explains the advantage over Defense-Prefix. These claims require additional controls or narrower wording.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant vulnerability with a simple, interpretable intervention: suppressing selected attention-head contributions to the CLS token without gradient-based fine-tuning.

The reported improvements are substantial and consistent across five OpenCLIP model sizes and four typographic benchmarks. ImageNet-100-Typo gains range from 13.14 to 19.60 percentage points, while clean classification accuracy is largely preserved on three datasets.

Layerwise probes, attention analysis, and controlled attention interventions provide complementary evidence that selected heads contribute to typographic susceptibility. Testing through ViT-BigG strengthens the empirical scope.
weaknesses: The central score is incorrectly specified. In Equation 6, the attention term in the numerator cancels the identical denominator, leaving a count of masked tokens independent of the head. The dataset sum also lacks normalization despite the claimed range of [0,1]. This may be a notation error, but the published definition cannot produce the reported rankings and needs correction to make the method reproducible.

The mechanistic evidence does not establish typography-specific circuit discovery convincingly. Scores are computed using text at a fixed bottom-center location, without matched no-text or non-text-overlay controls to separate typography sensitivity from positional preference. Random-head, layer-matched, and alternative-ranking ablations are absent. The interventions establish a causal contribution of the selected heads, but do not establish that the proposed score uniquely identifies the relevant mechanism.

The defense comparison is insufficient for the state-of-the-art competitiveness claim. Only Defense-Prefix is evaluated, on ViT-L, despite several other defenses being discussed. Defense-Prefix outperforms the proposed method on all three attacked benchmarks in Table 4, including 82.78% versus 65.00% on Disentangling. Better clean-task retention is useful, but no matched robustness–utility comparison or runtime measurement establishes the overall advantage.

Safety-critical deployment claims exceed the evaluation. Experiments cover zero-shot classification under existing attacks, without adaptive attacks, downstream VLM jailbreak tests, or generative-system evaluations. Section 7 correctly acknowledges that applications using spatial tokens may retain typographic information, which substantially limits the asserted suitability as a broad drop-in defense.

Reproducibility and uncertainty reporting are inadequate. The manuscript omits exact pretrained checkpoint identifiers, detailed probe training and evaluation protocols, complete synthetic-text generation settings, and repeated-run or confidence-interval results. These omissions matter particularly for the 110- and 180-image benchmarks. A model release is claimed, but no accessible release location is provided.

Several internal inconsistencies undermine confidence in the presentation: Figure 5's caption reverses the alpha convention used in Equation 8 and the results discussion; Table 3 and Table 4 report different ViT-L Aircraft improvements; and the abstract's less-than-1% ImageNet-100 degradation claim overlooks the reported 1.06-point decline for ViT-G.

The inference that MLPs discard information is stronger than the analysis supports. Reduced linear-probe accuracy and fewer PCA components explaining 95% of variance can reflect changes in accessibility or representation geometry rather than information loss. These observations do not justify excluding MLPs from the mechanistic account.

weaknesses: The security evaluation omits adaptive attacks and incorrectly argues that non-differentiability makes them infeasible. Adaptive evaluation can use discrete or black-box search over text content and rendering choices. Performance on fixed attacks therefore does not establish robustness against an attacker aware of the defense.

The mechanistic contribution lacks essential controls. Scoring heads using text fixed at the bottom of images can confound typography sensitivity with positional preferences. There are no matched non-text overlays, randomized-location scoring controls, or comparisons against random and layer-matched head ablation under the same selection procedure. Consequently, the added value of the proposed attention score over accuracy-guided pruning remains unclear.

Baseline evidence does not establish a compelling robustness advantage. Appendix J shows OCR-and-blur outperforming Dyslexify on ImageNet-100-Typo for every model, by up to 10.80 percentage points, while largely preserving clean accuracy. Its inference-cost disadvantage is not quantified. Defense-Prefix is evaluated for accuracy on only one model, and other cited defense families are not compared; Defense-Prefix also substantially outperforms Dyslexify on Disentangling.

Several interpretations exceed the evidence. Lower linear-probe accuracy and fewer principal components explaining 95% variance do not establish that MLPs discard information. Manipulating all spatial attention in selected heads establishes behavioral influence, but does not isolate text-specific information transmission or establish a complete typographic circuit.

Reproducibility and experimental reporting need improvement. Exact pretrained checkpoints, probe-training details, and several attack-generation settings are insufficiently specified; variability across attack realizations and circuit-selection samples is not reported. Table 5's total head counts conflict with the layer/head grids in Figures 12–15, undermining the reported sparsity percentages. Figure 5's caption also reverses the direction of the intervention described correctly in the main text.

The safety-critical deployment claims are premature. The medical experiments do not clearly establish disjoint circuit-selection and evaluation data or address overlap among ISIC2019, HAM10k, and BCN20k. Aggregate accuracy alone does not characterize malignant-lesion sensitivity. More broadly, the defense targets CLS representations, while many motivating multimodal applications consume spatial tokens and are not evaluated.

strengths: The paper proposes a useful, interpretable intervention: selectively suppressing attention-head contributions to the CLS token without gradient-based fine-tuning.

The empirical improvements are substantial and consistent across five CLIP model sizes and several synthetic and real typographic benchmarks. ImageNet-100-Typo gains reach 22.06 percentage points, with small clean ImageNet-100 accuracy changes.
The attention interventions provide evidence that the selected heads causally influence typographic sensitivity, going beyond correlations from linear probes alone.
The appendices strengthen the evaluation through OCR capability measurements, runtime comparisons, an OCR-and-blur baseline, and an exploratory medical application.
weaknesses: The defense evaluation omits adaptive attacks, and the stated justification that non-differentiability makes adaptive evaluation infeasible is incorrect. Adaptation does not require differentiability; query-based search over text and rendering choices remains possible. Consequently, the experiments establish improvements against fixed benchmarks, not robustness against attackers targeting the defense.

The mechanistic contribution lacks essential controls. The attention score is measured with text always in the bottom two token rows, potentially conflating positional preference with typography specialization. There are no matched non-text overlays, randomized-location controls, or comparisons against random-head and alternative-ranking selection under the same greedy search. Because circuit construction explicitly selects heads that improve attacked accuracy, the results do not isolate the added value of the proposed score.

Competitive positioning is incomplete. Table 9 shows that OCR plus blur outperforms Dyslexify on ImageNet-100-Typo for every model, by up to 10.80 percentage points, while largely preserving clean accuracy. Avoiding recurring OCR computation is a legitimate advantage, but its inference-time benefit is not quantified. The learned-defense comparison covers only Defense-Prefix on ViT-L and three real attack datasets, with a substantial loss on Disentangling; other cited defenses are not evaluated.

The causal interpretation exceeds the evidence. Manipulating selected heads establishes their influence on predictions but does not demonstrate a complete or specifically typographic circuit. Likewise, reduced linear-probe accuracy and lower PCA effective dimensionality do not establish that MLPs remove information; they can reflect changes in accessibility or representation geometry.

The medical evidence does not substantiate deployment-oriented safety claims. Circuit selection uses ISIC2019, but evaluation splits and handling of overlap with HAM10k and BCN20k are not documented sufficiently to establish independent transfer. Overall accuracy alone also leaves clinically important malignant-case sensitivity, specificity, and calibration unexamined.

Important evaluation and reproducibility details remain unclear, including exact pretrained checkpoints, probe training protocols, evaluation partitions, and variability across attack-generation seeds. Confidence intervals are particularly relevant for the 110- and 180-image real-attack datasets. Claims that smaller construction subsets yield comparable results are not supported with quantitative experiments.

The scope and presentation need correction. The intervention protects CLS representations while leaving spatial-token pathways available, limiting the broad VLM and safety-critical drop-in claims, as the limitations section acknowledges. Figure 5's caption reverses the direction of the alpha intervention relative to its equation, plot, and main text. Overall, the promising benchmark gains do not outweigh the unresolved defense-evaluation and mechanistic-validation gaps for a top-tier acceptance.

strengths: The paper offers a useful connection between mechanistic analysis and intervention: selectively suppressing attention-head contributions to the CLS token improves robustness without gradient-based fine-tuning.

The empirical gains are substantial and consistent across five model sizes and six typographic benchmarks. ImageNet-100-Typo improves by 16.74–22.06 percentage points, while clean ImageNet-100 accuracy changes by less than one point.
Attention interventions provide evidence that the selected heads causally influence typographic predictions, going beyond correlations from linear probes alone.
The appendices provide valuable additional evaluation, including OCR capability losses, computational costs, a preprocessing baseline, and a medical application.
weaknesses: The defense lacks adaptive evaluation. The claim that such evaluation is infeasible because typography is non-differentiable is incorrect: adaptive search need not use gradients. Consequently, the experiments establish robustness to existing attack distributions, but do not adequately support the broader adversarial robustness and safety-critical deployment claims.

The mechanistic contribution is insufficiently isolated. Head selection combines attention scores with supervised accuracy-based search, but there are no matched random-head, layer-matched, or accuracy-only selection baselines. Moreover, estimating scores using text fixed at the bottom of images can confound typographic selectivity with positional preference. The interventions demonstrate causal influence, but do not establish that the proposed score uniquely identifies a specialized typographic circuit.

Comparative evidence is mixed and incomplete. Appendix J's OCR-and-blur baseline outperforms Dyslexify on ImageNet-100-Typo for every model size, including 79.56% versus 68.76% for ViT-G, while largely preserving clean accuracy. Its inference-cost disadvantage is not quantified. Defense-Prefix is evaluated on only one model size, wins substantially on Disentangling, and other cited defense families are not compared experimentally.

The medical evaluation needs clearer separation between circuit-selection and evaluation data, and explicit handling of overlap among ISIC2019, HAM10k, and BCN20k. Aggregate accuracy without class-sensitive metrics or uncertainty is inadequate evidence for safety-critical utility. The separate 'Melanoma' dataset in Table 4 is also not clearly documented.

Reproducibility and reporting contain material gaps. Exact pretrained checkpoints, probe-training details, and several dataset splits are insufficiently specified; repeated-run uncertainty is absent. Table 5 reports 288 total heads for ViT-L, whereas Figure 12 depicts 24 layers with 16 heads, implying 384. Figure 5's caption reverses the direction of the alpha intervention relative to Equation 10 and the results.

The scope of the conclusions exceeds the experiments. Only CLS-based classification is defended, and the paper acknowledges that spatial-token consumers may remain vulnerable. Substantial OCR losses further restrict replacement suitability. These limitations, together with the missing controls and adaptive evaluation, leave the contribution below the acceptance threshold despite its promising empirical gains.
